trigger.summary: What starts a run: by hand, on a schedule, on a task event, when a session is restored, by polling a connection, or on a webhook. config.triggerType picks which.

triggerType.description: Runs when someone starts it, or execute_workflow

contextual.description: Offered from a task card or terminal right-click, inheriting its folder, branch and worktree as {{context.*}}

inputs.description: Parameters asked for before each run, read as {{inputs.<key>}}

key.description: Identifier the value is read by, as {{inputs.<key>}}

label.description: What the run dialog calls this field

type.description: Which control the run dialog shows, and how a supplied value is checked

required.description: A run cannot start without a value

defaultValue.description: Used when the run supplies nothing. A number must be finite, a boolean "true" or "false", a select one of its options

options.description: Choices for a select; a select without any is refused

placeholder.description: Hint shown in an empty field

description.description: Help text shown under the field

triggerType.description: Runs once at a set time

runAt.description: When to run, as an ISO 8601 date-time

timezone.description: IANA zone the cron is read in, e.g. "Europe/Madrid". Defaults to the machine

triggerType.description: Runs when a task is created; the task is {{task.*}}

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

triggerType.description: Runs when a task moves between statuses; the task is {{task.*}}, the move {{trigger.fromStatus}} and {{trigger.toStatus}}

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

fromStatus.description: Only when it leaves this status

toStatus.description: Only when it enters this status

triggerType.description: Runs when a session comes back after a quit, crash or reboot; {{trigger.restore}} says cold or warm

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

restore.description: cold (default): only when a process starts again. any: also when a pane reattaches to one still running

concurrency.description: perProject (default) runs one at a time per project, so restored sessions do not race for one port

triggerType.description: Polls a connection on a cron and runs once per new item; the item is {{connectorItem.*}}

event.description: Event type from the connector's manifest, e.g. issueCreated (list_connector_actions shows them)

cron.description: How often to poll, as a five-field cron expression

timezone.description: IANA zone the cron is read in

triggerType.description: Runs when the local webhook route receives a request; its body, headers and query are {{trigger.*}}

token.description: Secret path segment; a request without it is refused. Use a long random string

rules: A workflow has exactly one trigger, and no edge points into it.
A manual trigger may declare inputs; each is read anywhere as {{inputs.<key>}}, and execute_workflow takes their values.
What the trigger carries is read as {{task.*}}, {{trigger.*}} or {{connectorItem.*}}, depending on its type.

launchAgent.summary: Starts an AI coding agent in a project with a prompt. Headless, it runs in the background and the run waits for its answer; otherwise it opens a terminal tab.

agentType.description: Which agent CLI runs. fromTask uses the task's assigned agent, so it needs a task in scope (a task trigger, taskId or taskFromQueue)

model.description: Model passed to the CLI as written, e.g. "opus". Needs a concrete agentType

projectName.description: Registered project the agent works in, by name (list_projects)

projectPath.description: That project's absolute path; templates such as {{context.projectPath}} work

prompt.description: What the agent is asked to do. Templates expand before it is sent

headless.description: Run in the background and wait for it to finish, so later steps can read its output. Without it the agent opens in a terminal tab and the run does not wait on its answer

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema its final answer must match (headless only). Each top-level property becomes {{steps.<slug>.<field>}}; an answer that does not match fails the step

timeoutMs.description: How long a headless run may take before it is killed and the step fails, in milliseconds. Defaults to the app setting

worktreeMode.description: Where it works: none (the project folder), new (a fresh git worktree), fromStep (the worktree an earlier step made), existing (existingWorktreePath)

worktreeFromStepSlug.description: For worktreeMode fromStep: slug of the earlier agent step whose worktree to reuse

existingWorktreePath.description: For worktreeMode existing: absolute path of the worktree to work in

useWorktree.description: Older switch for a new worktree; prefer worktreeMode. fromContext inherits it from a contextual manual trigger

branch.description: Branch to check out or create for the worktree

args.description: Extra command-line arguments for the agent CLI

displayName.description: Name shown on the session tab

remoteHostId.description: Run on this remote host instead of this machine

promptDelayMs.description: Wait this long after the agent starts before sending the prompt, in milliseconds

taskId.description: Task the session is attached to

taskFromQueue.description: Take the project's next todo task and attach the session to it

outputs.description: Each top-level property of config.outputSchema, parsed from the answer (headless only)
The directory the agent worked in

rules: outputSchema requires headless: true, and an answer that does not match it fails the step.
Read typed fields in a condition, e.g. variable {{steps.review.approved}} equals true, rather than matching words in output.
agentType fromTask needs a task in scope: a task trigger, taskId or taskFromQueue. model needs a concrete agentType.
worktreeMode fromStep reuses the worktree of the earlier agent step named by worktreeFromStepSlug.

script.summary: Runs a bash, python, node or powershell script.

scriptContent.description: The script. Templates expand before it runs, so quote them as data. Its stdout is {{steps.<slug>.output}}; a non-zero exit fails the step

cwd.description: Directory it runs in. Defaults to projectPath

projectName.description: Project the script belongs to, by name

projectPath.description: That project's absolute path, used as the working directory when cwd is unset

secretsFrom.description: Connection whose stored secrets become this script's environment variables at run time, so no secret is written into the workflow

runId.description: Set by the engine; leave it out

outputs.description: What the script printed to stdout

rules: Templates expand into the script text before it runs. Keep a value as data rather than code, e.g. inside a quoted heredoc: cat <<'EOF' ... EOF.
A non-zero exit fails the step.
secretsFrom names a connection whose secrets become environment variables, so no secret is written into the workflow.

condition.summary: Compares a value, usually a step output, and sends the run down its true or its false branch.

variable.description: The value to test, usually a template such as {{steps.review.approved}}

operator.description: How variable is compared with value. Comparisons are on text

value.description: What variable is compared with; ignored by isEmpty and isNotEmpty

rules: Give it two outgoing edges, one with conditionBranch "true" and one with "false". Steps on the branch not taken are skipped.
Comparisons are on text: equals true matches the text "true".
Inside a loop body, both branches must stay inside the body.

approval.summary: Pauses the run until a person approves or rejects, in the app or with resolve_gate. It can show a review page, let the reviewer rewrite some text, and send the work back with a comment.

message.description: The question the reviewer is asked. Templates expand when the gate opens

timeoutMs.description: Reject automatically after this long, in milliseconds. Omit to wait for ever

view.description: A review page shown beside the question: HTML, or the path of a .html file, with templates filled in when the gate opens

edit.description: Text the reviewer may rewrite, as a template. Later steps read the result as {{steps.<gate>.text}}. When it expands to a JSON list of records the reviewer sees a table, and the rows they keep are {{steps.<gate>.items}}

feedback.description: Lets the reviewer send the work back with a comment instead of only approving or rejecting; the comment is {{steps.<gate>.feedback}} to the steps that redo it

from.description: Id of an earlier step, outside any loop body, that leads to this gate. Send back re-runs everything from it to the gate

maxRounds.description: How many times the gate may ask, the first included (2 to 10)

outputs.description: The editable text as the reviewer left it
When the editable text is a JSON list of records: the rows the reviewer kept, as a list, ready for a forEach loop
Comments pinned to the review page in the latest round, as a JSON list of {quote, comment, anchored}
The general note from the latest round
Every note, one line per round
Which time the gate asked, from 1

rules: A gate cannot sit inside a loop body.
When edit expands to a JSON list of records the reviewer sees a table; a rewrite that is no longer valid JSON is refused.
feedback.from is the id of an earlier step that leads to this gate, not the trigger and not a step inside a loop. Sending back re-runs every step from it to the gate. maxRounds is 2 to 10.
A reject ends the run.

createTaskFromItem.summary: Creates a task from the connector item that started the run, or updates the one it created before.

project.description: Project the task lands in, by name, or fromConnection to use the connection's execution project

initialStatus.description: Status of a newly created task. Re-syncing an existing one never changes its status

outputs.description: Imported or Updated, with the item id and title

rules: Needs {{connectorItem.*}}: put it after a connectorPoll trigger.
Re-syncing an item updates its title and description but never its status.

callConnectorAction.summary: Runs one action of a connected service (a comment, an issue, a merge...) with arguments built from templates.

connectionId.description: Connection the action runs against, from list_connections

action.description: Action type from the connector, e.g. commentOnPullRequest; list_connector_actions lists them with their args

actionLabel.description: The action's display name, for the canvas

connectorId.description: Connector the action belongs to, for a step placed before a connection exists

args.description: The action's arguments by name, every value a string template; a list or object a template names arrives as JSON text. list_connector_actions gives each action's args

outputs.description: Each field the action declares in its outputSchema; list_connector_actions gives them

rules: connectionId comes from list_connections; action and its args from list_connector_actions.
A step waits, rather than fails, when its connection needs signing in again.

httpRequest.summary: Sends one HTTP request, optionally through an http connection that adds auth.

url.description: Absolute URL, or a path resolved against the profile's base URL. Templates expand

headers.description: Request headers. Names are literal; values are templates

body.description: Request body as a template; empty sends none

profileConnectionId.description: An http connection whose base URL and auth are applied server-side, so no credential sits in the workflow

outputs.description: HTTP <code>, e.g. "HTTP 404": the way to read the response status
success or error: the step's own status, which replaces the response code under this name

rules: Put credentials in an http connection (profileConnectionId), not in headers.

Any answer succeeds, a 4xx or 5xx included: to act on the code, test {{steps.<slug>.output}} (e.g. contains "HTTP 2"). Only a network error or the 30 second timeout fails the step. Redirects are not followed.

loop.summary: Runs a group of steps (its body) several times: repeat up to 10 passes, stopping early when until holds, or forEach once per item of a list.

mode.description: repeat (default) runs the body up to maxIterations times; forEach runs it once for each item of items, with no cap on how many

items.description: For forEach: the list to walk, as a template naming it, e.g. {{steps.gate.items}}. JSON text of a list works too, and so does an object holding exactly one list. Each pass reads its item as {{loop.item}} or {{loop.item.<field>}}

bodyNodeIds.description: Ids of the steps the loop runs each pass. Wire them with edges: loop -> the entry steps, then between body steps, and from the last body steps to the step after the loop

maxIterations.description: For repeat: how many passes at most, a whole number from 1 to 10. Required for repeat, ignored for forEach

until.description: Checked after each pass; the loop stops early once it holds, e.g. {{steps.review.approved}} equals true

variable.description: The value to test, usually a template such as {{steps.review.approved}}

operator.description: How variable is compared with value. Comparisons are on text

value.description: What variable is compared with; ignored by isEmpty and isNotEmpty

outputs.description: How many passes ran, as a number
How many passes were planned: maxIterations, or the number of items
Per pass: {index, item?, status, steps: {<slug>: {output, status, error, ...}}}; each output cut to loopResultOutputChars
Per pass, the output of the last body step that ran (on the branch taken), cut to loopResultOutputChars

rules: bodyNodeIds lists every step in the body. Wire the loop to each body entry step, body steps to each other, and the last body steps to the step after the loop.
Nothing outside the loop may point into its body; only the loop starts its steps.
A body cannot hold an approval gate, a trigger or another loop, and cannot contain a cycle.
repeat needs maxIterations, 1 to 10. forEach needs items and has no cap.
Body steps read {{loop.item}} / {{loop.item.<field>}} (forEach), {{loop.index}} from 0, {{loop.number}} from 1 and {{loop.count}}.
A body step that fails ends the loop there, unless that step has onError: continue.
Inside the body, {{steps.<slug>.*}} of a body step is this pass. After the loop, read the passes through {{steps.<loop>.results}} or .outputs.

source.description: Id of the node that runs first

target.description: Id of the node that runs after it

conditionBranch.description: On an edge leaving a condition: which outcome takes it. Wire both. Omit on every other edge

templates.syntax: {{namespace.path.to.field}} anywhere a config takes text. An unknown namespace is left as written; a known one with nothing there becomes empty. Text longer than templateTextChars keeps its end.

namespaces.steps: {{steps.<slug>.<field>}}: the output of an earlier step, by its slug; the fields are listed under each node type
namespaces.task: {{task.title}}, .description, .id, .status, .branch, .projectName: the task a task trigger fired for
namespaces.trigger: {{trigger.*}}: what the trigger carried: fromStatus/toStatus, restore, or a webhook body, headers and query
namespaces.connectorItem: {{connectorItem.title}}, .body, .externalId, .externalUrl: the item a connectorPoll trigger fired for
namespaces.inputs: {{inputs.<key>}}: the values a manual run was started with
namespaces.context: {{context.cwd}}, .projectPath, .projectName, .branch, .worktreePath: where a contextual manual run was started from

config.message: Keep the findings worth a comment, and delete the rest.

config.scriptContent:
cat <<'EOF'
What each finding came to:
{{steps.loop.outputs}}
EOF
